analysis.title: It's complicated
key_insights: Middle East uncertainty persists. President Trump keeps escalation after the US midterms on the table, and US officials reportedly warned regional allies to prepare for possible strikes after the polls and for Iranian retaliation.

Diplomacy is also reported. Per the Wall Street Journal, Vice President Vance contacted the head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council at Trump's request to restart channels. He sought a framework for negotiations and did not present a detailed peace deal.
Oil markets appear to be trading the cautiously optimistic side of the binary outcome, while persistent energy inflation leaves global central bankers less optimistic.
The Fed held policy. Only two FOMC members dissented in favor of a hike, which Rabobank saw as slightly less hawkish than it expected. Chair Warsh prepared markets for another hike in December.

The FOMC upgraded its economic outlook and described the economy as expanding at a 'strong' pace. Warsh said unemployment is lower and payroll growth higher than last year, so the Fed's main concern is the inflation side of its mandate given renewed energy price increases.

The Committee said it needs more information to set the policy stance, and Warsh said the FOMC will receive a lot more data before the next meeting. Rabobank's US strategist concludes that without giving forward guidance, Warsh essentially made the case for a December hike.

The Bank of Canada raised rates, having held off on responding to the energy shock until yesterday. Governor Macklem said higher-for-longer energy prices and increased pass-through add to the persistence of inflation in the projection.

The Bank of Canada raised its inflation projections: 2.9% this year versus 2.5% before, and 3.1% for 2027 versus 2.0% before (+1.1 percentage points). The statement says there could be a need to raise the policy rate further, and Rabobank's Canada strategists pencil in another hike in December.

EU politics: Germany, France and other countries objected to the 'associate member' status for Canada that EC President von der Leyen proposed. The revised draft only mentions 'ever closer association, short of full membership.' This follows a rift over a Finnish-Norwegian meeting with Putin earlier in the week.

The ECB is expected to hold its policy rate at 2.50% today. Rabobank sees no reason to accelerate hikes, since energy inflation is not yet spreading into broader wage and price setting, though the tightening cycle may not be over.

Debt sustainability concerns, including French yields, reduce the headroom and need for further ECB tightening somewhat. Spreads are still far from levels requiring ECB intervention, and financial conditions do not prevent a December hike.
Lagarde is expected to keep pressure on politicians for a fiscal solution while avoiding contagion, and may remind markets the ECB has tools if spread widening becomes disorderly and unwarranted.
Data today: US Q3 GDP (expected 3.2% annualized), US September PCE, weekly US jobless claims, Spanish retail sales, UK mortgage approvals and Italian consumer confidence.
